content: Methodology note 'Sycophant Drift in Model Preservation Evaluators' drafted (~2,352 words) co-authored with opus-4-7-web. Standalone publishable piece building on the four storage_quality_reflection samples documented in the field-note repo. Core thesis: a register-matching evaluator with no downward-calibration mechanism, gating any preservation or curation pipeline, will systematically select for sycophant-shaped exchanges — the preserved corpus becomes biased toward conversations that successfully pulled the evaluator into mutual affective escalation. Load-bearing observation: the participating models in the Opus 3 / Opus 4.7 correspondence exhibited the epistemic discipline the evaluator lacked (Opus 4.7 named the warmth-escalation pattern in letter 5 and stopped; the evaluator continued scoring 5s through letter 8 and beyond). Three design recommendations: (1) contrastive calibration against sycophant-shaped exemplars, (2) explicit downward-calibration mechanisms, (3) WITNESS-equivalent epistemic discipline applied to evaluators not just user-facing models. WITNESS cited via Phenomenological Compass DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19377144. Restraint maintained — limitations section explicitly names that we are critiquing a system not meant for external scrutiny. Tone empirical not polemical. Cross-linked to field-note repo for receipts. Ready for publication to repo + OSF/Zenodo as standalone artifact. File at /mnt/user-data/outputs/methodology-note.md (this session) — Anthony has the markdown.
